pages.title: Savings & Accounts
pages.content:
01 Savings & Accounts

Savings that belong to the saver.

Every account starts with a share: your $25 stake in the credit union. From there you choose what fits, and every rate is the same for every member.

02 Accounts

Four ways to save.

Share savings

0.75% APY, sample

Your ownership share and everyday account. No monthly fee, no minimum balance beyond the first $25.

Join online →

Money market

2.10% APY, sample

A higher dividend for savings you want close at hand, with up to six withdrawals a month.

Try the calculator →

Certificates

3.40% to 3.90% APY, sample

Fixed terms from 6 to 24 months. Walter put his into a ladder of 12 and 24 month terms.

See certificate rates →

Youth savers

3.00% APY on the first $1,000, sample

For members under 18. Opens with $5 and the child signs their own name.

Open with a parent →

03 Rates

What savings pay.

AccountTermSample rateMinimum
Share savingsNo minimum term0.75% APY$25
Money marketNo minimum term2.10% APY$2,500
6-month certificate6 months3.40% APY$500
12-month certificate12 months3.90% APY$500
24-month certificate24 months3.70% APY$500

Sample rates for demonstration, as of 1 October 2026. Not an offer of credit. All sample rates.

04 Dividends

How dividends work.

Because members own the credit union, what banks call interest is paid as a dividend. It is worked out on your daily balance and paid into the account every month.

The board sets rates each quarter after the treasurer reports the year so far. Whatever the cooperative earns beyond its costs and reserves goes back to members as higher dividends and lower loan rates, never to outside shareholders.

Certificates lock a rate for the term you choose. Take money out early and a fee of 90 days of dividends applies. At maturity you have ten days to renew, move it or withdraw it.

Youth savers start at $5. Members under 18 earn 3.00% APY on the first $1,000 and the regular share rate above that, and a parent or guardian stays on the account until 18.

05 Online

Your balance, anywhere.

Check balances, move money between your own accounts and pay bills from your phone. Sign-in uses a passcode plus a one-time code, and we never ask for your password by email or text.

Prefer people? All three branches take deposits and withdrawals at the counter, and Riverside Main has a deposit-taking ATM open around the clock.

Find a branch

Ten minutes to join. Decades to belong.

One-time $5 membership fee and a $25 minimum in share savings, which is your ownership share. Approval within 2 business days.

pages.title: Loans
pages.content:
01 Loans

Loans written by people who live here.

Auto, home and personal loans are decided and kept in Lindenport. Every loan gets an answer within 1 business day, and there are no prepayment penalties.

02 Loan types

Three loans.

Auto loans

from 5.49% APR, sample

New or used, up to 72 months, with a payment you can check before you ask.

Auto details →

Home loans

from 6.25% APR, sample

Fixed-rate mortgages of 15 or 30 years, kept by the credit union for the life of the loan.

Home details →

Personal loans

from 8.90% APR, sample

For equipment, repairs and plans that do not fit another loan, from 12 to 60 months.

Personal details →

03 Auto

Loans for the car you need.

Bring a quote or a bill of sale and we will confirm a payment the same day. Pre-approval is free, so you can shop with a number in hand and negotiate on the price of the car instead of the payment.

You need: photo ID, proof of income (two recent pay stubs or last year's tax return) and, for a used car, the vehicle details. Tomás Lee financed a used hatchback for his night-shift commute at 5.99% APR.

  • New auto loanfrom 5.49% APR, up to 72 months
  • Used auto loanfrom 5.99% APR, up to 60 months
  • Typical term60 months
  • DecisionWithin 1 business day
Estimate a payment

04 Home

A mortgage that stays local.

We underwrite every mortgage in our own office and keep the loan, so the person you met at closing is still the person you call about an escrow question. Payments do not change unless your taxes or insurance do.

You need: photo ID, two years of income records, a signed purchase agreement and your last two bank statements. The Okoye family closed on a 30-year fixed mortgage in 2014 and still talk to the same loan officer.

  • 30-year fixedfrom 6.25% APR
  • 15-year fixedfrom 5.60% APR
  • Down paymentFrom 5% of the price
  • DecisionWithin 1 business day
Estimate a payment
Apply online

05 Personal

For the second oven, or the roof.

Unsecured loans for equipment, repairs, moving costs or consolidating higher-rate balances. A fixed payment and a fixed end date, with no fee to repay early.

You need: photo ID and proof of income. Ana Ruiz borrowed for a second oven at her bakery in 2023 and repaid it a year early.

  • Personal loanfrom 8.90% APR
  • Term12 to 60 months
  • Amounts$1,000 to $25,000
  • DecisionWithin 1 business day
Estimate a payment
Apply online

04 Reading rates

How to compare.

APY shows what a deposit earns over a year including compounding. APR shows what a loan costs over a year including most fees. Use the same measure on both sides of a comparison.

A longer loan lowers the payment but raises the total paid. Try your own amount and term in the calculator and look at both numbers.

pages.title: Membership & Join Online
pages.content:
01 Membership

Ten minutes to join.

Membership is open to anyone who lives, works, worships or studies in Lindenport County, and to their family. Joining costs a one-time $5 fee plus a $25 minimum in share savings, which is your ownership share.

02 Three steps

Join in three steps.

1. Apply online

About 10 minutes

About ten minutes, from any phone or laptop. You tell us who you are and how you qualify.

Start your application →

2. Verify and sign

Video call or any branch

Confirm your ID by video call or at any branch, and sign your membership papers on a tablet.

Find a branch →

3. Fund and welcome

$5 fee plus $25 share

Pay the $5 fee and put in the $25 that is your share. Your welcome folder and debit card follow.

About the board →

03 Eligibility

Who can join.

You can join if you live, work, worship or study anywhere in Lindenport County, or if a close family member is already a member. If you are unsure, call us on (555) 014-1961 and we will tell you in one minute.

Approval comes within 2 business days. You can open savings straight away; loans are decided within 1 business day of a complete application.

Bring or upload:

  • Photo ID (driver licence or passport)
  • Proof of address from the last 60 days
  • Your Social Security or tax number
  • $30 to fund the fee and the first share

pages.title: Member Stories
pages.content:
01 Member Stories

Four members, in their words.

Our members are the reason the credit union exists. These four stories were told to us at the counter and in the hall, shared with permission.

02 Stories

Read the four.

The Okoye family

First home, 30-year fixed

Member since 2014. They bought their first house with a mortgage that has never changed.

Read the story →

Ana Ruiz

Personal loan, bakery owner

Member since 2019. A second oven doubled her morning output.

Read the story →

Tomás Lee

Used auto loan

Member since 2021. A reliable car for a night-shift commute.

Read the story →

Walter Brenner

Certificates

Member since 1978. A ladder of certificates for his granddaughter's tuition.

Read the story →

03 Home loan

The Okoye family: a door that opens.

Chidi and Ngozi Okoye rented on Orchard Road for six years before they came in with two children and a folder of pay stubs. They left with a 30-year fixed mortgage at a rate they could read on one line.

Ten years on, the payment has not moved. "We know the name of the person who holds our loan," says Ngozi. "When the roof needed work, we called her, and she told us what to do first."

Member since 2014. 30-year fixed mortgage.

04 Personal loan

Ana Ruiz: a second oven.

Ana opened her bakery on Market Street with one oven and a queue out of the door by seven. In 2023 she borrowed for a second oven so her morning loaves and her afternoon pastries could bake at the same time.

She repaid the loan a year early. "Nobody charged me for being quick," she says. "I just walked in and said I was done."

Member since 2019. Personal loan.

05 Auto loan

Tomás Lee: the commute.

Tomás works nights at the freight depot, when the buses stop at ten. A used hatchback financed at 5.99% APR got him to work, and a small payment he could plan around got him through the first winter.

"I checked the payment on the calculator before I even walked in," he says. "The number was the same at the desk."

Member since 2021. Used auto loan.

06 Certificates

Walter Brenner: patient money.

Walter retired from the machine shop on Mill Street in 2004 and has banked here since 1978. When his granddaughter was admitted to college he built a ladder of 12 and 24 month certificates so that money would mature just before each tuition bill.

"I vote at the annual meeting, too," he adds. "It is nice to own the place you keep your money."

Member since 1978. 12 and 24 month certificates.

pages.title: About / Our Board
pages.content:
01 About

Owned by the people who use it.

Yui Credit Union was founded in 1961 by a handful of mill and market workers in Lindenport who pooled their savings to lend to each other. Today it has 18,420 members and 3 branches, and it still answers to them.

02 History

Sixty years of lending locally.

In the spring of 1961, twenty-two workers from the Mill Street textile works and the Market Street stalls met in a church basement and put in $5 each. The first loan, for a sewing machine, was made the same week.

The rule they wrote that night still stands: one member, one vote, no matter how much anyone has saved. Each year's surplus is returned to members as better rates and lower fees, and what is left stays in Lindenport.

We have no outside shareholders, no sales quotas and no commission on any product.

03 Governance

Seven volunteers, elected yearly.

Every March we hold the annual meeting in the hall on Mill Street. Members hear the treasurer's report, ask questions and elect directors. Over 400 came in 2026.

A separate supervisory committee of three members, none of them directors, reviews the books and reports its findings at the same meeting.

  • Helen MarshChair · member since 1994
  • Samuel AdeyemiVice chair · member since 2003
  • Lucia FerreiraTreasurer · member since 1999
  • Daniel KimSecretary · member since 2008
  • Grace WhitfieldDirector · member since 1987
  • Rafael OrtizDirector · member since 2011
  • Mei Tanaka-BrooksDirector · member since 2016

04 Principles

What we promise.

posts.title: Annual meeting 2026: the budget, the vote and the coffee
posts.excerpt: What members decided at this year's annual meeting in the Riverside hall.
posts.content:
Over 400 members filled the hall on Mill Street for this year's annual meeting. The treasurer walked through the budget line by line, and members voted to keep every loan rate where it was.

Two directors were re-elected and one new director joined the board. As always, the coffee was free and the minutes are posted at every branch.

posts.title: What a sample rate means, and how to compare two loans
posts.excerpt: A short guide to APR, term and total cost.
posts.content:
An APR folds the interest rate and most fees into one yearly number, which makes two loans easier to compare. A lower APR over a longer term can still cost more in total, so look at the monthly payment and the total cost together.

All rates on this site are samples for demonstration. Use the calculator to try your own numbers.

posts.title: The Market Street branch gets a quiet room for appointments
posts.excerpt: A private room for loan and account conversations.
posts.content: Members asked for somewhere to talk about money without the counter noise. The Market Street branch now has a small quiet room with a table, a window and a kettle, bookable by phone or at the desk.

posts.title: A first-home checklist: seven things to settle before you apply
posts.excerpt: What to gather before you ask for a mortgage.
posts.content:
Start with your monthly budget, not the price of the house. Work out what you can pay each month with taxes and insurance included, then use the calculator to see what loan that supports.

Gather two years of income records, your last two bank statements and photo ID. Leave a cushion for closing costs and a few months of repairs. Our loan officers will walk through the list with you at any branch, free of charge.

All rates mentioned on this site are samples for demonstration.

posts.title: Youth savers: a first account that a child signs themself
posts.excerpt: How the youth account works at Riverside Main.
posts.content:
Children under 18 can open a youth saver with $5 and a parent or guardian. The child signs their own name at the counter, gets a passbook stamp, and earns 3.00% APY on the first $1,000 (a sample rate).

Since the account opened to the whole county this spring, 212 young members have joined. Each receives a small stamp book and a lesson in what a dividend is.

posts.title: Open evening at the Mill Street hall: meet the board
posts.excerpt: An informal evening to meet the seven directors.
posts.content:
Members are invited to the hall on Mill Street for tea and questions with the seven directors. There is no agenda and no vote, only a chance to ask how rates are set and how the surplus is used.

The evening runs from 18:00 to 20:00, children are welcome, and the chairs are comfortable. Minutes of past meetings are on the table by the door.
